title: Airbnb Cleaning Checklist for Hosts and Cleaners (2026)
summary: Room-by-room Airbnb cleaning checklist with turnover times by bedroom count, linen par levels, photo steps, and the November 2026 checkout rules.
body_markdown:
An Airbnb turnover clean starts with photos of every room as the guest left it, then strips the beds and starts laundry, works top to bottom room by room, and ends with floors, restocking and a final photo walkthrough. Budget the time by bedroom count. Copy the room-by-room checklist below into your own document and hand it to your cleaner.


## What does Airbnb require hosts to clean between guests?


Airbnb's[ground rules for hosts](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2895) require every listing to be cleaned between every stay, including doing laundry, taking out trash, vacuuming or sweeping, and wiping surfaces. Properties must be free of health hazards such as mold and pests, and free of extensive dust, pet dander, and dirty dishes before check-in. Guests evaluate those exact points in Airbnb's[cleanliness rating prompt](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/1257) , and Airbnb notes in its[hosting cleaning guide](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes/a/clean-like-a-pro-with-these-expert-tips-663) that lack of cleanliness is one of the most common reasons a listing earns fewer than five stars.


Under Airbnb's[Rebooking and Refund Policy](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2868) , a guest has 72 hours from discovery to report a listing that is not reasonably clean and sanitary. When Airbnb approves a refund for a cleanliness issue, the host's payout is reduced by the refund amount. A dirty arrival also tends to show up in the written review, which every future guest can read; see what guests write in[Airbnb review examples for hosts](https://www.conduit.ai/blog/airbnb-review-examples-for-hosts) .


Airbnb's[cleaning supplies page](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes/a/stock-up-on-these-cleaning-supplies-189) still references its 2020 5-step enhanced cleaning process, though the enforceable policy today is the ground rules for hosts. That supplies page recommends using disinfectants registered with an agency such as the US EPA and letting each disinfectant stay wet on the surface for the contact time printed on the label. Vinegar and essential oils are not approved disinfectants, and cleaners should never mix bleach and ammonia.


## What order should an Airbnb turnover clean follow?


An Airbnb turnover clean goes fastest when laundry starts right after the arrival photos, because the washer and dryer set the pace, and floors come last, so dust and foot traffic don't land on finished work. Use this eight-step order on every checkout. The room order can follow your floor plan as long as laundry stays early and floors stay at the end.


1. Walk through every room and take arrival photos before touching anything to document any damage, open windows to air out the unit, and check for items guests left behind.
2. Strip all used beds, collect used towels and bath mats, check linens for stains, and start the first wash load immediately per[Airbnb's turnover checklist](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes/a/ensuring-your-place-is-sparkling-clean-570) .
3. Empty every trash bin and recycling bin, carry bags to exterior bins, and load or wash any dirty dishes left in the sink.
4. Clean and disinfect the kitchen from upper cabinets and appliances down to countertops and the sink.
5. Scrub and disinfect bathrooms from mirrors, counters, and fixtures down to showers, tubs, and toilets, giving EPA-registered disinfectant its full wet contact time.
6. Dust bedrooms and living areas from high shelves and blinds down to furniture, make beds with fresh linens, and lint roll the bedding.
7. Vacuum carpets, rugs, and hard floors, then sweep and mop hard flooring from the farthest room back toward the entry door.
8. Restock linens and consumables, run a final photo walkthrough, lock all doors and windows, and change the lockbox or smart lock entry code between reservations per[Airbnb's home safety guidance](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2809) .


## What goes on a room-by-room Airbnb cleaning checklist?


A room-by-room short-term rental cleaning checklist gives the cleaner one task per line with an exact verb, such as disinfecting the refrigerator handles after wiping the shelves. Copy the list below and stock a dedicated cleaner kit with an EPA-registered disinfectant, glass cleaner, all-purpose cleaner, microfiber cloths, scrub pads, a pumice stone, a toilet brush, a vacuum, and a microfiber mop. Keep a grill brush on site if there is a barbecue, plus a step ladder for high shelves and light fixtures and an extended duster for corners and cobwebs.


### Arrival and damage check


- Photograph every room from the doorway before moving or cleaning anything
- Open windows to air out stale odors instead of spraying heavy air freshener
- Inspect walls, furniture, linens, and rugs for stains, burns, or breakage
- Check under beds, inside drawers, and in closets for guest belongings
- Test lights, Wi-Fi router, TV, and thermostat to confirm everything works
- Inspect corners, ceilings, and under sinks for pests, cobwebs, or mold
- Press test buttons or check indicator lights on smoke and carbon monoxide detectors
- Report any damage or missing inventory to the host with close-up photos before cleaning


### Kitchen


- Empty the refrigerator and freezer completely, leaving no leftover food or open condiments
- Wash and sanitize refrigerator shelves, drawers, door bins, and interior walls
- Disinfect refrigerator handles, oven handles, dishwasher controls, and faucet levers
- Scrub the inside of the microwave, including the turntable and ceiling
- Empty toaster crumb trays and wipe down the toaster exterior
- Empty used coffee grounds, wash the carafe or drip tray, and wipe the coffee maker
- Degrease the stovetop, range hood filter, backsplash, and oven interior as needed
- Wash, dry, and put away all dishes, utensils, and cookware after inspecting for stuck food
- Wipe cabinet doors, drawer fronts, and inside cutlery trays to remove crumbs
- Disinfect countertops, island surfaces, and dining prep zones
- Scrub the sink basin and polish the faucet to remove water spots
- Empty trash and recycling bins, disinfect bin lids, and insert fresh liners
- Place a new kitchen sponge in its unopened wrapper next to the sink


### Bathrooms


- Strip all used bath towels, hand towels, washcloths, and bath mats
- Remove hair from shower, tub, and sink drains
- Scrub the shower walls, tub, glass doors, and grout lines to remove soap scum and mold
- Disinfect the toilet bowl, rim, seat, tank, base, and flush handle
- Clean and disinfect the vanity countertop, sink basin, and faucet handles
- Polish mirrors with glass cleaner until streak-free
- Wipe inside drawers, medicine cabinets, and cabinet doors for stray hair and dust
- Disinfect light switches, doorknobs, and exhaust fan switches
- Refill hand soap, shampoo, conditioner, body wash, and toilet paper to par level
- Vacuum and mop the floor, then hang fresh towels and place a clean bath mat once the floor is dry


### Bedrooms


- Strip pillowcases, sheets, and duvet covers and check mattress protectors for stains
- Inspect mattresses, bed frames, and headboards for pests, dust, or damage
- Check under beds and sweep or vacuum the full floor area underneath
- Wipe inside nightstand and dresser drawers and remove any trash or forgotten items
- Dust blinds, windowsills, lampshades, shelving, and framed artwork
- Disinfect light switches, doorknobs, alarm clocks, and bedroom TV remotes
- Make beds tightly with stain-free, pressed linens and arrange pillows to your photo guide
- Lint roll all made beds, pillowcases, and throw blankets to remove stray hair
- Straighten bed skirts, curtains, and closet hangers, leaving space for guest clothing
- Vacuum carpets or mop hard floors from the far corners toward the doorway


### Living and dining areas


- Vacuum sofa cushions, armrests, and underneath removable cushions for crumbs and hair
- Fluff and arrange throw pillows and fold throw blankets consistently
- Dust bookshelves, media consoles, blinds, ceiling fan blades, and indoor plants
- Disinfect TV remotes, game controllers, light switches, thermostats, and door handles
- Clean interior glass on windows, sliding doors, and wall mirrors
- Wipe dining table, chair backs, and seat cushions, checking for sticky spots
- Organize board games, guest welcome book, and visible cords neatly
- Store any host personal items out of sight in locked owner closets
- Vacuum rugs and hard floors, then damp mop hard flooring last


### Laundry


- Sort stained linens aside for pre-treatment instead of sending stains through the dryer
- Wash sheets, pillowcases, towels, and bath mats on the hottest fabric-safe cycle
- Clean the dryer lint trap before and after every load
- Wipe washing machine rubber door seals and detergent dispenser trays
- Disinfect washer and dryer control panels and door handles
- Fold and stack spare clean linens inside the linen closet at par level
- Sweep and mop behind and around laundry machines for lint and spilled detergent
- Check laundry detergent, stain remover, and dryer sheet inventory for the restock form


### Outdoor areas


- Sweep the front entry, porch, stairs, and patio clear of leaves and dirt
- Wipe down patio tables, chairs, and railings and brush off outdoor cushions
- Scrape barbecue grates with a grill brush, empty the grease tray, and check propane levels
- Clear cobwebs from exterior light fixtures, doorways, and eaves with an extended duster
- Pick up cigarette butts, bottle caps, and yard debris around walkways and parking spots
- Clean exterior glass on entry doors and sliding patio doors
- Secure outdoor umbrellas, pool gates, and storage boxes
- Confirm exterior walkway lights work and house numbers are visible from the street


### Final walkthrough


- Confirm the entire property smells clean and neutral after closing aired-out windows
- Verify every trash bin is empty with a fresh bag and all dirty laundry is cleared
- Check that every room matches your reference appearance photos
- Reset the thermostat to your between-stay temperature setting
- Turn off unnecessary interior lights, ceiling fans, and small appliances
- Confirm smoke and carbon monoxide detectors show normal status
- Capture required post-clean completion photos across every room
- Submit the supply restock form if any consumable or cleaning chemical is below threshold
- Lock all windows and exterior doors and update the smart lock or lockbox entry code


## How much should you restock at every turnover?


Turnover restocking starts with a linen par of 3 sets per bed: one on the bed, one clean in the closet and one in the laundry, so a same-day turnover never waits on the dryer.[Breezeway's linen program guide](https://www.breezeway.io/blog/vacation-rental-linen-program) (2024, with Inhaven's Ashley Ching) applies the same rule of three to towels: 3 fitted sheets and 3 flat sheets per bed, 3 pillowcases per pillow, 3 bath towels and 3 washcloths per occupant, 3 hand towels per bathroom, and 2 to 3 bath mats per bathroom.


Consumables depend on stay length and guest count, and no source publishes a standard. The quantities below are a starting point to adjust after a month of restock forms.


Consumable Starting quantity per turnover


Toilet paper 2 rolls per bathroom, plus 1 spare roll per bathroom per night booked


Hand soap 1 dispenser per sink, refilled below half


Dish soap 1 bottle per kitchen, refilled below half


Shampoo, conditioner, and body wash 1 full dispenser or set per shower


Dishwasher tablets 1 per night plus 2 extra


Coffee and filters 2 servings per adult guest per morning


Trash bags 1 liner in each bin plus 3 spares per bin


Paper towels 1 full roll on the holder plus 1 spare under the sink


Kitchen sponge 1 new sponge in its wrapper


Give cleaners a short restock form, on paper or a phone form, to fill in whenever a supply, light bulb or battery is below par, so you reorder before a guest runs out.


## How long does an Airbnb turnover clean take?


Airbnb turnover cleans take a median of 120 minutes in[ProhostAI's timed data](https://prohost.ai/blog/turnover-cleaning-time-benchmarks) , and bedroom count explains most of the difference between a short clean and a long one.[Breezeway's May 2026 report](https://www.breezeway.io/blog/how-long-does-vacation-rental-cleaning-take) , drawn from a platform that has handled more than 75 million tasks, puts the average job at about 3 to 5 hours depending on size. Both break the numbers down by bedroom count.


ProhostAI timed 30,985 cleans at 146 businesses and 2,249 listings between November 2025 and November 2026, counting only cleans where the cleaner tapped start and finish in the app. Its medians are 85 minutes for a studio or 1-bedroom, 106 for 2 bedrooms, 146 for 3, 165 for 4 and 201 for 5 or more. The slowest quarter of cleans starts at 132, 163, 230, 253 and 279 minutes for the same sizes. Half the checkouts in that data (49%) were same-day turnovers, with a median 5-hour gap to the next check-in, and 82% of same-day cleans finished in time.


Breezeway's averages by size are 2.99 hours (1 bedroom), 3.09 (2), 3.59 (3), 4.12 (4), 4.48 (5) and 4.92 (6). Breezeway says these are total job duration, not the combined hours of every cleaner, even though 2-bedroom and larger units are usually cleaned by several people at once. Part of the gap is the statistic: Breezeway reports an average, which a few very long jobs pull up, and ProhostAI reports a median. Plan from the median and keep the longer figure as your buffer.


### Worked example


Take a 2-bedroom rental with an 11:00 checkout and a 16:00 check-in, giving a 5-hour same-day window that matches ProhostAI's median. Plan the labor estimate around the 106-minute median, then buffer the schedule to 163 minutes (where the slowest quarter of 2-bedroom cleans starts) so a messy checkout does not trigger a late check-in. If the cleaner starts at 12:00, an hour after checkout (ProhostAI's median start is 63 minutes after checkout), a 163-minute clean finishes around 14:45. That leaves about 75 minutes to treat a stain, replace a broken lamp or sort out a lock before the 16:00 arrival.


## What photos should a cleaner take at every turnover?


Turnover photos should record the property twice: as the guest left it, before any cleaning, and as the next guest will find it, right before lockup. Airbnb asks for photos or videos as evidence for a Host damage protection claim, and the second set lets you check beds, bathrooms and restocked supplies from your phone before the next guest walks in. Take these seven sets at every turnover.


1. Wide shots of every room as found, which record the condition at checkout.
2. Close-up photos of any stain, scratch, breakage, or extra mess with an everyday object or ruler in frame for scale.
3. Each made bed photographed from the doorway to verify smooth linens and pillow placement.
4. Bathroom views showing the toilet, shower or tub, sink, mirrors, and stocked towels.
5. Kitchen countertops, stovetop, sink, and the inside of the empty refrigerator.
6. Restocked consumables and spare linens inside cabinets or closets.
7. Thermostat readout and locked doors or lockbox on exit.


Some cleaning software can require a photo before a cleaner ticks off a task.[Turno](https://turno.com/features/photo-checklists) includes Mandatory Checklist Completion, which requires time-stamped verification photos before a cleaner can mark an item complete.[Properly](https://www.getproperly.com/features/photo-checklists) requires photo proof before task completion and supports before-and-after photo pairs, with its Platform plan starting at $12.99 per property per month and Real-Time Inspection at $5 per inspection.[Breezeway](https://www.breezeway.io/checklists-mobile-app) provides per-property checklists in 10 languages with embedded reference photos, required completion photos, task time tracking, and GPS tracking.


## What can you ask guests to do at checkout under Airbnb's new house rules?


Airbnb's[updated house rules policy](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/4168) for reservations booked on or after November 20, 2026 says hosts are generally not allowed to ask guests to strip the bed, take trash off-site, or wash and put away dishes, though Airbnb may grant exceptions based on the listing and local rules. Hosts also generally cannot impose fines or other penalties, and every rule must be listed in the designated house rules section before booking rather than added afterward through messages or printed signs inside the property.


Airbnb's[policy update guidance](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes/a/important-changes-to-house-rules-21) lists requests hosts can still include as Additional rules: putting used dishes in the sink, gathering used towels, separating trash and recycling into indoor bins, and turning off the air conditioning. Airbnb is conducting initial listing reviews through March 2027 and gives hosts at least 20 days to update non-compliant rules or submit an appeal.


For the checklist, plan as if no guest strips a bed, washes dishes or carries trash to the outside bins. Budget cleaner time for all three on every checkout.


## What should you do when the cleaner finds damage at turnover?


Guest damage found during turnover needs photo and video proof before the cleaner touches it, followed by a payment request to the guest within 14 days of checkout and a full Host damage protection filing within 30 days of checkout. Under[Airbnb's Host damage protection](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/279) , Airbnb reimburses hosts up to $3 million for guest damage and unexpected extra cleaning caused by stains, pet accidents, smoke odor, or unapproved guests, while normal wear and tear and routine checkout cleaning (laundry, dishes, and trash) are excluded.


1. Stop cleaning that area, take photos and a short video, and keep itemized cleaning invoices, repair estimates or replacement receipts.
2. Pull inventory records for any damaged furniture or electronics, including make, model, and purchase date, to support valuation.
3. Open a reimbursement request with the guest in the[Airbnb Resolution Center](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/767) within 14 days of checkout and notify Airbnb.
4. Give the guest 24 hours to respond; if the guest declines or does not reply, ask Airbnb to step in.
5. Submit the complete Host damage protection payment request form with all supporting evidence within 30 days of checkout under the[Host damage protection terms](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2869) .


For bookings outside Airbnb, or to cover damage without filing a claim, compare[damage waivers vs. security deposits](https://www.conduit.ai/blog/vacation-rental-damage-waiver-vs-security-deposit) .


## How often should you deep clean a short-term rental?


Short-term rental properties need a scheduled deep clean every two to three months, according to[Airbnb's expert cleaning tips](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes/a/clean-like-a-pro-with-these-expert-tips-663) , because routine turnovers focus on visible surfaces and high-touch points rather than buildup behind appliances or on walls. Splitting the work into monthly, every-two-to-three-month and yearly jobs keeps each deep-clean day short enough to fit between bookings.


- Monthly tasks: sweep porches thoroughly, check under-sink plumbing for slow leaks, trim shrubs away from paths and windows, descale coffee makers and showerheads, and wipe ceiling fans and vents.
- Every two to three months: pull out large appliances to clean behind the refrigerator and stove, dust high furniture and cabinet tops with an extended duster, wash mattress protectors and duvet inserts, clean window tracks, and scrub tile grout.
- Yearly tasks: spot clean or wash scuffed walls, treat upholstery and rug stains, touch up chipped paint, and pressure wash decks or patios.


Add these jobs to the bottom of your checklist and give each frequency its own color (every turnover, monthly, every two to three months, yearly), so cleaners can work from one sheet.


## How do you hand this checklist to a cleaning team?


Handing a cleaning checklist to an outside crew works best with a reference photo guide: one photo of every room as it should look when finished, walked through with each new cleaner during onboarding. Run the clean once yourself before you hire, so you know how long it takes and where supplies belong, and line up a backup cleaner for the day your regular one can't come.


Rename the rooms on your copy of the list to match the home ("Upstairs bunk room" instead of "Bedroom 2") and swap in the actual products ("glass cleaner on the shower door, never the scrub pad"). Hand over the restock form on day one, and set up a message routine for[dispatching cleaners by text](https://www.conduit.ai/blog/dispatch-cleaners-contractors-sms-whatsapp) when checkout times shift.


Once turnovers run across several homes, the checklist, photos and restock forms are easier to keep in one system. Its AI inspections add-on, from $10 per unit per month, checks video walkthroughs against your checklist and turns issues into tasks. Details are on[Conduit's pricing](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing) page.


## FAQ


Two Airbnb documents set what a host can recover after a turnover and what a guest can be asked to do: the Host damage protection terms (last updated February 5, 2026), which set the 14-day and 30-day claim clocks, and the house rules policy for bookings from November 20, 2026, which limits checkout chores.


### How much time should I leave between checkout and check-in?


Leave at least the slowest-quarter clean time for your unit size, plus the cleaner's travel time. ProhostAI's same-day turnovers had a median 5-hour window and 82% of those cleans finished before the next check-in time, so a gap shorter than that needs a second cleaner or an earlier start.


### What color sheets and towels work best for an Airbnb?


White, because white linens can be washed hot and bleached, which is how stains come out between guests. Breezeway's linen guide suggests a T250 cotton and polyester blend (60/40 is common) and warns that 100% microfiber can't take high heat or bleach, and Airbnb's setup guide calls white towels the easiest to maintain.


### Can I charge a guest for leaving dirty dishes?


Usually not. Airbnb's house rules policy says hosts generally should not impose fines, and for bookings from November 20, 2026 hosts are generally not allowed to ask guests to wash and put away dishes. Host damage protection also excludes normal checkout cleaning such as dishes, laundry and trash, so build that work into your cleaning fee.


### Does Airbnb pay for a deep clean after a guest smoked inside?


Host damage protection can reimburse smoke odor removal when a guest smoked against your house rules, but you need evidence that the guest caused it. Airbnb's terms list photographs, professional assessments, smoke detector readings or the guest's own admission as examples, and Airbnb may require the cleaning invoice to come from an independent company it approves.


### Does Airbnb cover extra cleaning when a guest brings unapproved guests?


Yes. Extra cleaning required because of additional unapproved guests is on the list host damage protection covers. Ask the guest for payment through the Resolution Center within 14 days of checkout, and if the guest doesn't pay, file the full request with invoices and photos within 30 days of checkout.


### Can I send guests checkout instructions by message instead?


A message can remind guests of rules already on the listing, but it cannot add new ones. For bookings from November 20, 2026, Airbnb says house rules must be in the designated section of the listing before booking, not added later by message or sign, and it now offers your house rules as a pre-written quick reply for reminders.
